questions.text: Choose the correct form: She ___ to the market every morning.
questions.explanation: Third person singular present tense requires the -s/-es ending.

questions.text: Which of the following is an antonym of 'generous'?
questions.explanation: Stingy is the opposite of generous; it means unwilling to give or spend.

questions.text: Identify the error: 'Neither the teacher nor the students was present.'
questions.explanation: With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject (students = plural), so it should be 'were'.

questions.text: What does the idiom 'to burn the midnight oil' mean?
options: To work late into the night
questions.explanation: This idiom means to work or study late at night.

questions.text: Choose the correct preposition: She is interested ___ learning French.
questions.explanation: The correct prepositional phrase is 'interested in'.

questions.text: Which sentence is in the passive voice?
options: The ball was kicked by the boy.
The boy is kicking the ball.
The boy will kick the ball.
questions.explanation: The passive voice follows the pattern: subject + be + past participle (+ by agent).

questions.text: Choose the correct article: He is ___ honest man.
questions.explanation: 'An' is used before words starting with a vowel sound. 'Honest' begins with a vowel sound.

questions.text: What is the plural of 'child'?
questions.explanation: The plural of 'child' is 'children' (irregular plural).

questions.text: Choose the correct tense: By the time we arrived, they ___ already left.
questions.explanation: The past perfect tense ('had left') is used for an action completed before another past action.

questions.text: Which word is a conjunction in this sentence: 'He studied hard, ___ he passed the exam.'?
questions.explanation: 'And' is a coordinating conjunction connecting two clauses.

questions.text: Choose the correct indirect speech: He said, 'I am tired.'
options: He said he has been tired.
He said he will be tired.
questions.explanation: In reported speech, present tense shifts to past tense: 'am' becomes 'was'.

questions.text: What figure of speech is used in: 'Time is money'?
questions.explanation: This is a metaphor because it directly compares time to money without using 'like' or 'as'.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: The news ___ good.
questions.explanation: 'News' is an uncountable noun and takes a singular verb.

questions.text: Which sentence contains a punctuation error?
questions.explanation: 'He said stop' should have a comma and quotation marks: He said, 'Stop.' or He said, 'Stop!'

questions.text: Choose the correct conditional: If I ___ rich, I would travel the world.
questions.explanation: In second conditional sentences, 'were' is used for all subjects (subjunctive mood).

questions.text: Which word is an uncountable noun?
questions.explanation: 'Furniture' is uncountable; you cannot say 'a furniture' or 'furnitures'.

questions.text: What is the correct spelling?
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'accommodation' with double c and double m.

questions.text: Choose the correct modal: You ___ respect your elders.
questions.explanation: 'Should' expresses obligation or moral duty, which fits the context of respecting elders.

questions.text: In Nigerian English, what does 'chop' typically mean?
questions.explanation: In Nigerian English, 'chop' commonly means 'to eat'.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: One of the students ___ absent yesterday.
questions.explanation: 'One of the students' takes a singular verb because 'one' is the subject.

questions.text: Which word is an adverb?
questions.explanation: 'Quickly' modifies a verb and is formed with the -ly suffix, making it an adverb.

questions.text: Choose the correct tense: I ___ in Lagos since 2020.
questions.explanation: The present perfect tense is used with 'since' to indicate an action that started in the past and continues.

questions.text: What does the proverb 'A word is enough for the wise' mean?
options: A wise person needs only a hint to understand
questions.explanation: This proverb means that a smart person understands quickly without needing lengthy explanation.

questions.text: Choose the correct possessive form: The ___ car is parked outside.
questions.explanation: For singular possession, add 's to the noun: boy's.

questions.text: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: Each of the students have submitted their work.
Each of the students has submitted their work.
Each of the students have submitted his work.
Each of the students has submitted their assignment.
questions.explanation: 'Each' is singular and takes 'has'. 'Their' is now widely accepted as a singular gender-neutral pronoun.

questions.text: Choose the correct preposition: The teacher walked ___ the classroom.
questions.explanation: 'Into' indicates movement from outside to inside.

questions.text: Which sentence uses a simile?
options: The wind whispered through the trees.
questions.explanation: A simile compares two things using 'like' or 'as'. 'Eyes sparkled like diamonds' uses 'like'.

questions.text: Choose the correct tag question: She is a doctor, ___?
questions.explanation: A positive statement takes a negative tag: 'isn't she'.

questions.text: Which word is a countable noun?
questions.explanation: 'Dog' is countable: you can say 'a dog' or 'dogs'.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: The team ___ playing well this season.
questions.explanation: In standard British English, collective nouns like 'team' take singular verbs.

questions.text: What is the main idea of a passage usually found in?
questions.explanation: The main idea is typically expressed in the topic sentence, usually at the beginning of a paragraph.

questions.text: Choose the correct reported speech: 'Please close the door,' she said.
options: She said please close the door.
She asked to close the door.
She requested me to close the door.
She told me to close the door.
questions.explanation: Commands become reported speech with 'told + object + to + infinitive'.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a part of speech?
questions.explanation: 'Sentence' is a grammatical unit, not a part of speech.

questions.text: Choose the correct tense: If it ___ tomorrow, we will stay at home.
questions.explanation: In first conditional sentences, the if-clause uses the present simple tense.

questions.text: What does the idiom 'to spill the beans' mean?
questions.explanation: This idiom means to disclose secret information.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: The furniture in the room ___ new.
questions.explanation: 'Furniture' is uncountable and takes a singular verb.

questions.text: Which sentence has correct punctuation?
questions.explanation: No punctuation is needed between the verb and its complement in a simple sentence.

questions.text: Choose the correct preposition: The meeting is ___ Monday.
questions.explanation: We use 'on' with specific days.

questions.text: In a formal letter, which greeting is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: 'Dear Sir/Madam' is the standard formal greeting when the recipient's name is unknown.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: He suggested that she ___ early.
questions.explanation: After verbs like 'suggest', the subjunctive mood uses the base form of the verb.

questions.text: What is the synonym of 'abundant'?
questions.explanation: 'Abundant' means existing in large quantities; 'plentiful' is its synonym.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: Everybody ___ their own opinion.
questions.explanation: 'Everybody' is an indefinite pronoun and takes a singular verb.

questions.text: Which sentence uses the active voice correctly?
options: The homework was done by the student.
questions.explanation: In the active voice, the subject performs the action: 'The student did the homework.'

questions.text: Choose the correct conjunction: Study hard, ___ you will fail.
questions.explanation: 'Or' is used to express a consequence if the action is not taken.

questions.text: What type of noun is 'Lagos'?
questions.explanation: 'Lagos' is a proper noun because it is the name of a specific city.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: The children ___ playing in the park.
questions.explanation: 'Children' is a plural noun and requires a plural verb.

questions.text: Which word best completes: 'The professor gave a ___ on climate change.'
questions.explanation: 'Lecture' is the correct noun to complete the phrase 'gave a lecture on'.

questions.text: Choose the correct tense: They ___ dinner when the phone rang.
questions.explanation: The past continuous tense is used for an ongoing action interrupted by another event.

questions.text: What is the meaning of 'to hit the nail on the head'?
questions.explanation: This idiom means to describe exactly what is causing a situation or problem.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: Neither the principal nor the teachers ___ available.
questions.explanation: With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject 'teachers' (plural).

questions.text: Which word is a preposition?
questions.explanation: 'Under' shows the relationship of position between words.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: The woman who lives next door ___ a nurse.
questions.explanation: 'The woman' is singular and takes the singular verb 'is'.

questions.text: What is the purpose of a topic sentence?
options: To introduce the main idea of a paragraph
questions.explanation: A topic sentence introduces the main idea that the paragraph will discuss.

questions.text: Choose the correct indirect speech: He asked, 'Where do you live?'
options: He asked where do I live.
He asked where did I live.
questions.explanation: In reported questions, word order changes to statement order and tense shifts back.

questions.text: Choose the correct modal: You ___ have told me about the exam.
questions.explanation: 'Should have + past participle' expresses regret or criticism about a past action.

questions.text: Which sentence has a subject-verb agreement error?
options: The cat sleeps on the sofa.
questions.explanation: 'The boys' is plural and should take 'play', not 'plays'.

questions.text: What does 'to add insult to injury' mean?
options: To make a bad situation worse
questions.explanation: This idiom means to make a bad or unpleasant situation even worse.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: The news from the village ___ disturbing.
questions.explanation: 'News' is uncountable and always takes a singular verb.

questions.text: Which word is an adjective?
questions.explanation: 'Tall' describes a noun and is therefore an adjective.

questions.text: Choose the correct tense: She will have finished the project by tomorrow.
questions.explanation: 'Will have finished' is the future perfect tense, showing completion before a future time.

questions.text: In Nigerian English, what does 'dash' mean?
options: To give a tip or bribe
questions.explanation: In Nigerian English, 'dash' means to give money as a tip or bribe.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: The police ___ investigating the case.
questions.explanation: 'Police' is a plural noun in standard English and takes a plural verb.

questions.text: Which sentence correctly uses a semicolon?
options: I like tea; coffee is also good.
questions.explanation: A semicolon connects two related independent clauses: 'I like tea; coffee is also good.'

questions.text: Choose the correct form: A number of students ___ absent today.
questions.explanation: 'A number of' is followed by a plural noun and takes a plural verb.

questions.text: What is personification?
options: Giving human qualities to non-human things
questions.explanation: Personification gives human characteristics to animals, objects, or ideas.

questions.text: Choose the correct tense: I ___ this book before.
questions.explanation: The present perfect tense is used for experiences that happened at an unspecified time.

questions.text: Which word means the same as 'commence'?
questions.explanation: 'Commence' means to begin or start.

questions.text: Choose the correct preposition: The exam will commence ___ 9 a.m.
questions.explanation: We use 'at' with specific times.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: Either the students or the teacher ___ responsible.
questions.explanation: With 'either...or', the verb agrees with the nearer subject 'teacher' (singular).

questions.text: What is the plural of 'ox'?
questions.explanation: The plural of 'ox' is 'oxen' (irregular plural).

questions.text: Choose the correct form: The boy, together with his friends, ___ going to the cinema.
questions.explanation: The phrase 'together with' does not make the subject plural. 'The boy' is singular.

questions.text: Which is the correct sentence in standard English?
questions.explanation: 'Doesn't' (does not) is the correct negation for third person singular in standard English.

questions.text: Choose the correct tense: We ___ to Abuja next week.
questions.explanation: The present continuous can be used to express future plans.

questions.text: What does the proverb 'Unity is strength' mean?
questions.explanation: This proverb emphasizes that cooperation and togetherness lead to greater power.

questions.text: Choose the correct modal: He ___ be at home by now.
questions.explanation: 'Might' expresses possibility; it suggests he possibly is at home.

questions.text: Which sentence uses 'whom' correctly?
options: Whom is coming to the party?
Whom do you think will win?
questions.explanation: 'Whom' is the object form of 'who' and is correct after a preposition: 'To whom'.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: The books that I borrowed ___ interesting.
questions.explanation: 'Books' is plural and the relative clause describes it, so the verb must be plural.

questions.text: What is the antonym of 'ancient'?
questions.explanation: 'Ancient' means very old; 'modern' is its opposite.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: The number of applicants ___ increasing.
questions.explanation: 'The number of' is followed by a plural noun but takes a singular verb.

questions.text: Which is NOT a correct use of a comma?
options: Before the subject of a sentence
Before a coordinating conjunction joining two independent clauses
questions.explanation: A comma should not be placed between the subject and the verb of a sentence.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: She asked me ___ I could help her.
questions.explanation: 'If' is used to report yes/no questions in indirect speech.

questions.text: Which sentence has a dangling modifier?
options: Walking to class, the rain started.
She walked to class in the rain.
The rain started while she was walking.
Walking to class, she got wet.
questions.explanation: 'Walking to class' incorrectly modifies 'the rain' instead of a person.

questions.text: Choose the correct tense: By next year, I ___ here for five years.
questions.explanation: Future perfect tense is used for actions that will be completed before a future time.

questions.text: What does 'to cry over spilt milk' mean?
options: To waste time on something done
To be very sad about something
questions.explanation: This idiom means to waste time being upset about something that has already happened.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: The company have announced their results. (British usage)
options: This is correct in British English.
questions.explanation: In British English, collective nouns can take plural verbs when emphasizing individual members.

questions.text: Choose the correct preposition: She has been absent ___ Monday.
questions.explanation: 'Since' is used with a specific point in time to indicate the start of a period.

questions.text: Which word is a countable noun?
questions.explanation: 'Book' is countable: you can say 'a book' or 'books'.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: Every boy and every girl ___ entitled to education.
questions.explanation: When two singular subjects are connected by 'and' with 'every', the verb is singular.

questions.text: What is the tone of this sentence: 'The results were disappointing but not unexpected'?
questions.explanation: The sentence presents a balanced, factual observation without strong emotion.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: He made me ___ the truth.
questions.explanation: After causative verbs like 'make', the base form of the verb (infinitive without 'to') is used.

questions.text: In Nigerian English, what does 'flash' mean in phone context?
options: To call briefly so the person sees your number
questions.explanation: In Nigerian English, 'flash' means to make a brief call so the recipient sees your number.

questions.text: Choose the correct tense: If I had known, I ___ you.
questions.explanation: Third conditional: If + past perfect, would have + past participle.

questions.text: Which word is an abstract noun?
questions.explanation: 'Freedom' is an abstract noun because it refers to a concept, not a physical object.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: The scissors ___ on the table.
questions.explanation: 'Scissors' is a plural noun (like 'trousers') and takes a plural verb.

questions.text: What does the idiom 'break the ice' mean?
options: To initiate conversation in an awkward situation
questions.explanation: This idiom means to make people feel more comfortable in a social situation.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: The jury ___ reached a verdict.
questions.explanation: In standard English, 'jury' as a single body takes a singular verb.

questions.text: Which sentence correctly uses 'fewer'?
options: There are fewer water in the bottle.
There are fewer furniture in the room.
questions.explanation: 'Fewer' is used with countable nouns: 'fewer students'.

questions.text: Choose the correct tense: She has been working here ___ 2019.
questions.explanation: 'Since' is used with a point in time (2019) with the present perfect continuous tense.

questions.text: What is the correct way to address an envelope in formal writing?
options: Put the sender's address at the top right
Put the recipient's address at the bottom left
Put the recipient's address on the left side below the date
questions.explanation: In formal letter writing, the recipient's address goes on the left side.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: He is one of those people who ___ always complaining.
questions.explanation: The relative pronoun 'who' refers to 'people' (plural), so the verb is plural.

questions.text: Choose the correct preposition: The lecture is ___ grammar.
questions.explanation: We say 'a lecture on' a topic.

questions.text: Which sentence is a compound sentence?
options: Although it rained, we went out.
She studied hard, so she passed.
The boy who won is my friend.
Running quickly, he caught the bus.
questions.explanation: A compound sentence has two independent clauses joined by a coordinating conjunction.

questions.text: Choose the correct tense: I will call you when I ___ home.
questions.explanation: In time clauses with 'when', the present simple tense is used to refer to the future.

questions.text: Which word means 'to make something smaller'?
questions.explanation: 'Reduce' means to make something smaller in size, amount, or degree.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: Mathematics ___ one of the difficult subjects.
questions.explanation: 'Mathematics' is a singular noun and takes a singular verb.

questions.text: What does 'to call it a day' mean?
options: To stop working for the day
questions.explanation: This idiom means to stop working on something, usually for the rest of the day.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: A pair of shoes ___ lying on the floor.
questions.explanation: 'A pair of' is treated as singular because 'pair' is singular.

questions.text: Which word is a collective noun?
questions.explanation: 'Crowd' is a collective noun referring to a group of people.

questions.text: Choose the correct tense: He ___ already ___ when I arrived.
questions.explanation: Past perfect tense (had + past participle) shows an action completed before another past action.

questions.text: Choose the correct direct speech: She said that she was happy.
questions.explanation: When converting reported speech back to direct speech, the tense and pronouns revert to their original form.

questions.text: What type of clause is 'because she was tired'?
questions.explanation: 'Because she was tired' is an adverbial clause that modifies the main clause.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: Both the teacher and the students ___ present.
questions.explanation: 'Both...and' connects two subjects that together form a plural subject.

questions.text: Choose the correct preposition: She is afraid ___ snakes.
questions.explanation: The correct phrase is 'afraid of'.

questions.text: Which sentence contains a run-on?
options: She went to the market, and she bought food.
She went to the market she bought food.
Although she went to the market, she bought food.
She went to the market; she bought food.
questions.explanation: Two independent clauses are joined without any punctuation or conjunction.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: The police ___ looking for the suspect.
questions.explanation: 'Police' is always plural in standard English.

questions.text: What is the meaning of 'once in a blue moon'?
questions.explanation: This idiom means something that happens very rarely.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: Ten thousand naira ___ not enough.
questions.explanation: A sum of money is treated as a singular subject.

questions.text: Which word is an adverb of frequency?
questions.explanation: 'Always' tells us how often something happens, making it an adverb of frequency.

questions.text: Choose the correct tense: He will come if you ___ him.
questions.explanation: In conditional sentences, the if-clause uses the present simple tense.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: The herd of cattle ___ moving slowly.
questions.explanation: 'Herd' is the subject and is singular, so it takes a singular verb.

questions.text: What is a formal closing in a letter?
questions.explanation: 'Yours faithfully' is an appropriate formal closing when the recipient's name is unknown.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: She insists on ___ the work herself.
questions.explanation: The preposition 'on' is followed by the gerund (-ing form).

questions.text: Which sentence is in the active voice?
options: The cake was baked by my mother.
My mother bakes a cake every Sunday.
questions.explanation: In the active voice, the subject performs the action: 'My mother bakes'.

questions.text: Choose the correct preposition: He graduated ___ the University of Lagos.
questions.explanation: We say 'graduate from' an institution.

questions.text: What is the correct plural of 'medium'?
questions.explanation: The plural of 'medium' is 'media' (from Latin).

questions.text: Choose the correct tense: She would have come if she ___ invited.
questions.explanation: Third conditional: If + past perfect (had been invited).

questions.text: Which sentence correctly uses an apostrophe?
questions.explanation: 'Its' (possessive) has no apostrophe. 'It's' means 'it is' or 'it has'.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: Everyone ___ here except John.
questions.explanation: 'Everyone' is singular and takes a singular verb.

questions.text: What is hyperbole?
questions.explanation: Hyperbole is an extreme exaggeration used for emphasis or humorous effect.

questions.text: Choose the correct tense: The train ___ by the time we got to the station.
questions.explanation: Past perfect is used for an action completed before another past action.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: The species of fish ___ endangered.
questions.explanation: 'Species' is both singular and plural; here it is used as singular.

questions.text: Which word is a relative pronoun?
questions.explanation: 'Which' introduces relative clauses and refers back to a noun.

questions.text: Choose the correct indirect speech: He said, 'I will come tomorrow.'
options: He said he would come tomorrow.
He said he will come the next day.
He said he would come the next day.
He said he would come tomorrow.
questions.explanation: In reported speech, 'will' becomes 'would' and 'tomorrow' becomes 'the next day'.

questions.text: What does 'to beat around the bush' mean?
options: To avoid talking about the main topic
questions.explanation: This idiom means to avoid talking about what is important.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: The information in these documents ___ confidential.
questions.explanation: 'Information' is uncountable and takes a singular verb.

questions.text: Which sentence is correctly punctuated?
questions.explanation: No punctuation is needed between the subject and the verb in a simple sentence.

questions.text: Choose the correct tense: He ___ working since morning.
questions.explanation: Present perfect continuous is used with 'since' for actions that started in the past and continue.

questions.text: Choose the correct modal: You ___ smoke in the hospital.
questions.explanation: 'Must not' expresses prohibition, which is appropriate for hospital rules.

questions.text: What is an antonym of 'transparent'?
questions.explanation: 'Opaque' means not able to be seen through, the opposite of transparent.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: Mathematics and Science ___ compulsory subjects.
questions.explanation: Two subjects joined by 'and' form a plural subject.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: He suggested that the meeting ___ postponed.
questions.explanation: After 'suggest', the subjunctive mood uses the base form: 'be postponed'.

questions.text: In Nigerian English, what does 'return work' mean?
options: To come back to work after an absence
questions.explanation: In Nigerian English, 'return work' often means to resume duty after being away.

questions.text: Choose the correct tense: We ___ never ___ such a beautiful place.
questions.explanation: Present perfect tense is used for life experiences.

questions.text: Which word is a conjunction?
questions.explanation: 'Although' is a subordinating conjunction that introduces a dependent clause.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: The children ___ not ___ to go out.
questions.explanation: 'The children' is plural, and the passive form is 'are allowed'.

questions.text: What is the tone of this passage: 'Nigeria is a great country with abundant resources and hardworking people.'?
questions.explanation: The passage expresses pride and positive feelings about Nigeria.

questions.text: Choose the correct preposition: She is fond ___ reading.
questions.explanation: The correct phrase is 'fond of'.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: The manager, as well as his employees, ___ going to the conference.
questions.explanation: 'As well as' does not make the subject plural. 'Manager' is singular.

questions.text: What does 'to be on cloud nine' mean?
questions.explanation: This idiom means to be extremely happy or elated.

questions.text: Choose the correct tense: If I ___ you, I would apologize.
questions.explanation: In second conditional sentences, 'were' is used for all subjects.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: The pair of glasses ___ on the table.
questions.explanation: 'A pair of' is singular; the verb agrees with 'pair'.

questions.text: Which is the correct comparative form of 'good'?
questions.explanation: 'Better' is the comparative form of 'good' (irregular).

questions.text: Choose the correct form: Three-fourths of the work ___ completed.
questions.explanation: When a fraction refers to an uncountable noun ('work'), the verb is singular.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: He is taller ___ his brother.
questions.explanation: 'Than' is used after comparative adjectives.

questions.text: What does the idiom 'a blessing in disguise' mean?
options: Something bad that turns out to be good
questions.explanation: This idiom describes something that seems bad at first but results in something good.

questions.text: Choose the correct tense: She ___ to Lagos tomorrow.
questions.explanation: The present continuous can express a planned future action.

questions.text: Which sentence uses 'who' correctly?
questions.explanation: 'Who' is the subject form. In 'Who did you meet?', 'who' is the object of 'meet'.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: The data ___ analyzed by the researchers.
questions.explanation: 'Data' is technically plural (singular: datum) and takes a plural verb.

questions.text: Choose the correct preposition: He has been married ___ 10 years.
questions.explanation: 'For' is used with a period of time (10 years).

questions.text: What is the plural of 'cactus'?
questions.explanation: The plural of 'cactus' is 'cacti' (from Latin).

questions.text: Choose the correct tense: If I had studied harder, I ___ the exam.
questions.explanation: Third conditional: If + past perfect, would have + past participle.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: The news about the accident ___ very sad.
questions.explanation: 'News' is uncountable and takes a singular verb.

questions.text: Which word is an interjection?
questions.explanation: 'Well' can be used as an interjection to express surprise or hesitation.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: She enjoys ___ classical music.
questions.explanation: The verb 'enjoy' is followed by the gerund (-ing form).

questions.text: Which sentence has correct subject-verb agreement?
options: The group of students are ready.
The group of students is ready.
The group of students have been ready.
The group of students were ready.
questions.explanation: 'Group' is the subject and is singular; 'of students' is a prepositional phrase.

questions.text: What does 'to let the cat out of the bag' mean?
questions.explanation: This idiom means to accidentally reveal secret information.

questions.text: Choose the correct tense: I ___ waiting for you since 8 o'clock.
questions.explanation: Present perfect continuous is used with 'since' for ongoing actions.

questions.text: Choose the correct indirect speech: She said, 'Where is the hospital?'
options: She asked where was the hospital.
She asked where the hospital was.
She asked where is the hospital.
She asked where the hospital is.
questions.explanation: In reported questions, word order becomes statement order and the tense shifts back.

questions.text: Which sentence is a complex sentence?
options: She went to school and came back.
When the bell rang, the students rushed out.
He likes tea. She likes coffee.
questions.explanation: A complex sentence has one independent clause and at least one dependent clause.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: Neither of the answers ___ correct.
questions.explanation: 'Neither' is singular and takes a singular verb.

questions.text: What is the correct way to write a date in formal English?
options: All of the above are acceptable
questions.explanation: All three formats are acceptable in formal English writing.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: Each of the books ___ a different story.
questions.explanation: 'Each' is singular and takes a singular verb.

questions.text: Choose the correct tense: He ___ to the cinema yesterday.
questions.explanation: The simple past tense is used with 'yesterday'.

questions.text: What does the proverb 'A stitch in time saves nine' mean?
options: Fixing a problem early prevents it from getting worse
questions.explanation: This proverb means that solving a problem promptly prevents it from becoming bigger.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: The army ___ deployed to the north.
questions.explanation: Collective nouns like 'army' can be treated as singular when acting as a unit.

questions.text: Choose the correct modal: She ___ have passed the exam with such good grades.
questions.explanation: 'Must have + past participle' expresses strong certainty about a past event.

questions.text: Which word is a synonymous with 'commence'?
questions.explanation: 'Commence' means to start or begin.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: The students ___ asked to submit their assignments.
questions.explanation: 'Students' is plural and requires a plural verb.

questions.text: Which sentence contains a misplaced modifier?
options: She served cake to the children on paper plates.
On paper plates, she served cake to the children.
She served cake on paper plates to the children.
She served cake to the children.
questions.explanation: 'On paper plates' could modify 'children' instead of 'cake'.

questions.text: Choose the correct preposition: The book is ___ the shelf.
questions.explanation: We use 'on' for objects resting on a surface.

questions.text: Choose the correct tense: They ___ married for 20 years now.
questions.explanation: Present perfect continuous is used for ongoing states with 'for'.

questions.text: What is the tone of this statement: 'The policy has been a complete failure.'?
questions.explanation: The statement expresses strong disapproval of the policy.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: The furniture in the offices ___ brand new.
questions.explanation: 'Furniture' is uncountable and takes a singular verb.

questions.text: Which word is an article?
questions.explanation: 'The' is the definite article in English.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: The children ___ happy to go to school.
questions.explanation: 'Children' is a plural noun and takes a plural verb.

questions.text: Choose the correct tense: By the time the police arrived, the robbers ___ away.
questions.explanation: Past perfect is used for an action completed before another past event.

questions.text: What does 'to piece together' mean?
options: To assemble or gather information gradually
questions.explanation: This phrase means to assemble information or evidence from various sources.

questions.text: Choose the correct preposition: The train arrived ___ 3:00 p.m.
questions.explanation: We use 'at' with specific times.

questions.text: Which sentence has the correct use of 'affect' and 'effect'?
options: The effect of the policy was great.
The affect of the policy was great.
The policy was effected by the government.
questions.explanation: 'Effect' (noun) means a result. 'Affect' is usually a verb meaning to influence.

questions.text: Choose the correct tense: I ___ never ___ to China.
questions.explanation: Present perfect with 'never' expresses life experience up to now.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: The family ___ going on vacation next week.
questions.explanation: In British English, 'family' can take a plural verb when emphasizing individual members.

questions.text: What is an antonym of 'temporary'?
questions.explanation: 'Permanent' means lasting forever, the opposite of temporary.

questions.text: Choose the correct tense: He ___ already ___ his homework before I arrived.
questions.explanation: Past perfect tense is used for actions completed before another past action.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: The committee ___ decided on the new policy.
questions.explanation: When the committee acts as a single body, it takes a singular verb.

questions.text: Which sentence uses the correct form of 'there/their/they're'?
questions.explanation: 'They're' is the contraction of 'they are'. 'They're coming' = 'They are coming'.

questions.text: Choose the correct tense: I will wait until you ___ ready.
questions.explanation: In time clauses with 'until', the present simple tense is used for the future.

questions.text: What does the idiom 'to bite the dust' mean?
questions.explanation: This idiom means to be defeated, to fail, or to die.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: Neither of the students ___ present.
questions.explanation: 'Neither' is singular and takes a singular verb.

questions.text: Which sentence is a question tag?
options: I wonder if you are coming.
questions.explanation: A question tag is a short question added to a statement: 'aren't you?'

questions.text: Choose the correct form: Everybody ___ to be treated with respect.
questions.explanation: 'Everybody' is an indefinite pronoun and always takes a singular verb.
